about: Verse of the day. Day 1 is 'start' (viewer's local date); day N shows the Nth verse of 'text' in order. 'days' holds the hook, word of the day and reel for a verse id; anything missing is simply not shown. 'tags' are hashtags for every day's share and caption; a day may add its own 'tags'.
title: Meghadūta

1.1.hook: A lover in exile. A cloud as his messenger.

word.en: separation from the one you love
word.note: Inside the compound kāntā-viraha-guruṇā, “heavy with separation from his beloved”. The whole poem grows from it.

1.2.hook:
Months alone on a mountain.
Then, on the first day of the rains, a cloud.

word.note: Here megham, the cloud he sees clinging to the peak. The poem is named for it: Megha-dūta, the cloud messenger.

1.3.hook:
One look at a rain cloud,
and even a happy heart aches.

word.note: antar, within, and bāṣpa, tears: standing before the cloud, he holds his tears back.

1.4.hook:
He offers the cloud fresh flowers,
and a welcome.

word.note: su, well, and āgata, come: “well come”, the greeting he speaks to the cloud.

1.5.hook:
A cloud is only smoke, light,
water and wind.
Love doesn't care.

word.note: kāma, love, and ārta, afflicted: those in love plead with anything, living or not.

1.6.hook:
Better to ask the great and be refused
than to ask the small and succeed.

word.note: yācñā moghā varam adhiguṇe: a request refused by the noble is better.

1.7.hook:
His message has one address:
Alakā, city washed in Śiva's moonlight.

word.note: saṃtaptānāṃ tvam asi śaraṇam: “you are the refuge of the scorched.”

1.8.hook:
When the rain clouds come,
travellers' wives know
their husbands are coming home.

word.note: pathika-vanitāḥ, the travellers' wives, who look up at the cloud and take heart.

1.9.hook:
Hope is the thread that keeps
a loving heart from breaking.

word.note: āśā, hope, and bandha, bond: it holds a flower-soft heart through separation.

1.10.hook:
A gentle wind, a singing bird,
cranes in rows:
good omens for the journey.

word.note: The balākās fly in garlands beside the cloud, a delight to the eyes.

1.11.hook: Thunder, and the swans rise. They will fly with the cloud all the way to Kailāsa.

word.note: rāja, king, and haṃsa, swan: when the rains begin, they fly north to Lake Mānasa.

1.12.hook: Before leaving, the cloud embraces an old friend: a mountain marked by Rāma's footprints.

word.note: raghupati-padaiḥ, “by the footprints of the lord of the Raghus”: Rāmagiri, where Rāma once walked.
